Christmas Eve
The writer sat in the great living room on Christmas Eve. He was trying to write, but there was something coming up him. He found he had not much to say. His family came into his heart, those memories of Christmas with the family that he’d walked away from nearly two years ago.
The man texted his ex-wife (the mother of his children) and his kids:
Middle-aged-man:  I wish you all a Merry Christmas. I remember our first Christmas here in New Mexico in the little apartment at the new Mexico Children’s home. We were so thankful to God that we had a safe place to be and presents under the tree. I was so excited about Christmas morning that I think I woke up the kids myself to get the show going! I will always be grateful for all the times we had together. Merry Christmas, family. I love you.
He received no response.
The middle aged man sat in the tiled living room with his instruments. He was becoming acquainted with a loneliness. As the writer was attempting to write, a facebook notification appeared on the screen of his Chromebook. A friend had tagged him in a post. The lonely man clicked on the link. 
Ry Dalee John Jacob Jingleheimer Schmidt, by Travis Erwin. That was awesome. Almost as awesome as a Dr. Dave song workshop
The memory had come from a North Carolina retreat that the man had been blessed enough to attend twice (His way was paid for the second time and he’d been sent home with a rare guitar! Oh, the gifts that life had brought to this man!). The Wilcox Weekenders are a people who come together in Hendersonville, North Carolina every Spring to celebrate Love and Music with their host, David Wilcox, the beautiful man whose songs bring us all together.
This post reminded him of a joyful moment that he’d shared with his friends at Kanuga. The man was reminded of the connectedness that he’d experienced in that moment. Nonetheless, the middle aged man felt alone in his loneliness. 
The man, in his desire to be seen in that moment, made a post of his own on the closed group page:
“In the past two years I have stepped away from my marriage and my job and so much of the false-self. I've been to one psychiatric unit and two treatment centers, and today I am sheltered through the generosity of a friend. I am so grateful for all the love, all the support. I am so grateful for all of you, my friends. I had to step up to the edge to really experience you, to really see you, to really feel you. I take this moment to express how grateful I am for what I can see here from the edge. It is absolutely breathtaking. What a view...if you ever have the chance, I recommend it. The miracle is this, I am now holding the suffering and the joy simultaneously. It's not one or the other any more. It's BOTH AND. Much love to you!”
As he published his post, his phone rang. It was Dan. The man wept with gratefulness as he put the phone to his ear. He allowed his true state to be felt and heard in the presence of his trusted friend.
“Hey, Dan,” the man said, tears audible in his voice.
“Hey, bud, me and Christy wanted to invite you over for a Christmas Eve get-together.”
The man accepted the invitation. He gathered the left over sparkling cider and root beer from the lovely lunch that he’d had with his children earlier that day. He also grabbed a loaf of hard crusted bread. Dan, texted from the driveway, “I’m here.”
The man walked outside wearing his olive jacket and carrying his humble offerings. He was embraced in the loving arms of what-is that night. He was held by the Great Mother. He was supported in the fabric. He found himself in community. The man was loved, and the man had experienced that Love many, many ways. 
But love never comes the same way twice. We find our love today in novel ways. Love comes to us unexpected. And if we are offended and disturbed by that which is unexpected then we may miss our love. Great Mother, open our hearts up for the novel expression of Love in our lives today.
The friends broke bread. The friends drank cold sweet drinks and warm tea. The woman of the house prepared a dip for the broken bread. The piano was played. The guitar was strummed. Voices were raised in song. Gifts were given—and there was even one for the middle-aged-man! 
The man did not stay too long. He did not stay too short. He stayed until he was ready to go, then Dan took him back home.
The man was watching the miracle of Christ child being born in his life. He was giving birth to the Christ daughter. He participated in the forms that presented themselves to him. He was saying “yes” to life. The man was coming to know himself as the very Life that he longed for. He was held. And, there was so much more holding to come, dear reader! So much more awakening to witness. So much more Universal being for us to discover together, dear reader. Come! Come! As Christmas morning awaits! 
Come! Come! Whoever you are. Wanderer, Worshipper, lover-of-leaving.

3:13 AM
Christmas morning
“Awe is the capacity to let the other be the other without having to appropriate and incorporate it into the ego.”
        Bruce Sanguin
With the coming and going of Christmas Eve, and the arrival of an early Christmas morning, the dying author felt. The author sat in the tiled living room, his laptop right where it was designed to be (in his lap), coming to grips with the what was happening in his being. “Do I write about this sense of loneliness? This sense of alienation? Is that the path today?” he presented his question to the Universal.
The writer (this dying author, the one who prayed for his own death that you may live, dear reader) –The writer was reminded of the non-path. He wondered if that had anything to do with him right now. He was only vaguely aware of the miracles that he’d reported thus far in his wiritings which spanned the previous week. 
He breathed in. He breathed out. He remembered his audience. “Is that what a dying author does?” he thought to himself. He sat, facing North, his fingers curled over home-row.
“Is this what Shakespeare meant when he said that all the world is a stage?” he wondered. The dying author acknowledged the comfort that he felt as he was immersed in his work, the comfort he felt in his writing. He found comfort as he cultivated his relationship with his audience, even as his audience may be currently unaware that he was addressing them.” He wondered if they were aware though, somehow. “Maybe this book has already been read,” the writers heart soared with that possibility, “Maybe this book has already been written and is being read by you, dear reader, right now.” What a joyful meditation it was for the writer! “Praise be to the reader who is being born again in our Presence, Mother! None of us are alone!”
They were out there. Those “others.” And just like that, the miracle had happened again. The miracle of non-aloneness that he’d just discovered in the acknowledgment of his audience. He scrolled back up to the words from Bruce Sanguin that he’d transcribed just minutes ago. He wondered, “How do we allow the other to be other? How do we allow the other to be other without incorporating them (he scrolled up again)…without appropriating them into the ego? He wondered if he knew anything about what Bruce was talking about here. He didn’t want to miss that, so he went back to the reading.
Sanguin goes on to speak about these peak experiences that we have as humans, these mountain top experiences that we have, these mystic experiences, and he exhorts his audience to give them as much attention as possible. 
“Bruce is giving me permission to let these peak experiences guide my life. Thank you Bruce, for giving me the gift of my birth in your writings! Thank you for dying that death, so that I may now live. Thank you for embodying the Universal Christ!” 
Bruce postulates that we may have some kind of hangover from the rising of the age of reason, that our “robot” (left() brain may have taken over our beings, and that this is why the world seems like “one damn thing after another.” The medicine, he says, allows us to connect more deeply with our right brain experience, the reality of the poet and the artist and the dancer, that part of us who experiences the world in its sensory fullness, that part of us who experiences the world in all its connectivity and one-ness. He goes on to speak about one of his medicinal experiences:
“…After the serpent moves through my body in the ceremony, I am directed to put my hands together in the prayer position, place my thumbs on my forehead and bow toward my heart. Try it. Hold this postion for thirty seconds or more. You may discover one or more of the following things happen: less thinking; no thinking at all; deeper, more rhythmic breathing; a sense of calm; absence of worry; feelings of gratitude.”
            Bruce Sanguin, Dismantled
Dear reader, the dying author, in his participation with Bruce’s suggestion, is once again reconnected to Source. I am the Author who has died who is now willing to speak through all of us. Who is this being, you may ask, who is speaking? He is the one who is deepest within you. 
Bruce, one of the Chiefs (those kachinas) who, for years and years, said “yes” to the form. He left his form behind. He dropped his nets in order to follow. He left behind that which he knew in order to follow, in order to go deeper into the Being-ness of it all. Thank you, Bruce. I give you thanks.
The writer (the wildly talented writer?) realized that he’d unconsciously crossed over into a genuine expression of first person as he’d finished that last paragraph. He left it there, just as it was. Let it be an altar. “Is this what the death of the author is?” he wondered. This genuine expression of first person.” The I AM. “The I AM is in first person, isn’t it?” he thought to himself. He found company in Self. He found company in that genuine expression of first person.
“Dear, Mother,” the man prayed. “Will you help me to acknowledge the “other” without incorporating them into my ego? Is that possible? Can I witness the “other” without appropriating them? Will you allow me, Great Mother to stop re-traumatizing myself and the “other” in this way? Open my eyes, Mother to the ways in which I appropriate the “other.”
The time was now 4:12 AM. It had taken the author fifty-nine minutes to find his breath. Fifty-nine minutes to find his Love. Fifty-nine minutes to find his Self. Fifty-nine minutes to fall in love. Fifty-nine minutes to leave behind his misery. To leave behind his suffering. Fifty nine miutes to see this miracle come to pass. Praise be to the snake that moves through us, the ONE who circles back!
The writer sat in awe and reverence with his hands in prayer position, thumbs on his forehead, experiencing his own breathe, the Yaweh, the name that cannot be spoken, the Presence. His breathing slowed. He allowed himself to fall into that deep trance that he’d discovered when he’d become the snake as a seven year old boy. When he’d been transformed, slithering on his belly up to his parents room, and down the laundry chute to the basement, where he curled up into that deep meditation. That deep ophidian sense of stillness.
The stillness was profound. He was able to be with his breath intimately here. “What a gift, to have made peace with the snake,” he thought. What a journey. What a long journey. To make peace with that which the world thought to be the Satan. He sat with that thought. Surprised by the fear. “The serpent? Should I be saying that? The one who scares us? The Satan? The one who was damned to crawl on his belly. Wasn’t he already crawling on his belly? Wasn’t that his nature? What does it mean to be that low? To be that in touch with the earth? How grounded is that? Maybe we are just afraid of being on my belly in the grass. Maybe we are just afraid to return to the earth from which we came.”
Who are the entities who threaten us? Are they out there? If the snake is not my enemy, then who is? What is this genuine expression of first person? Who am I? Who are you? Are we here together? Audience? Deceased author? Is this what it means to be an author who has undergone this dying process (made peace with the snake). 
The author who has died can walk in other realms. The author who has died is free to be with you here. Now. The author who has died is not bound to his laptop in one particular moment in time. The author who has died is free. The author who has died is with you now, the audience, accompanying you in your death and resurrection journey. “Her I am. My dear?”
There it was. The author, in his attempt to type Here I am, had actually typed “Her I am.” And there she was. The one who was been rising up. He felt a tingling in his kundalini region. There She is. There I am. And this is how we arrive here together, in this very fluid state of being, where we are no longer holding on to these very fragile identities, where we allow ourselves to flow in and out, just as fluid as we need to be. The author, once again, brought his hands together in prayer position, his thumbs on his forehead, he bowed to his heart…Her heart.
Is it true that there is no male or female in Christ? Who wrote that, and what was happening there? Maybe I’m missing the point here. I mean, is this about me becoming a woman? Is this about me coming out of the closet? Is this about having sex with men. Is this about putting on women’s clothes? Is that what I’m coming to here? Or is this about something deeper than that expression (not that there’s anything wrong with that! Seinfeld! LOL)? But really, is this about something deeper than a man pretending to be a woman? Or maybe I just don’t understand the depths of what it means when a man dresses up like a woman. What am I giving myself to here? I do not know. But, right now, I trust. I trust. I am facing the unknown as I allow this “Her” to arise from within.
Maybe the “Her” is not a her at all. Maybe the Her is a construction. Maybe the Her is one side of the binary in the evolution of all consciousness. I’m not saying that male and female are strictly constructions, obviously there are differentiated sex organs. That’s hard to get around. But, that which is inside of us, is it not that which is much more fluid than we (i) have allowed it to be? Is this what I’ve been trying to make peace with all of my life, that my children’s generation seems to be more comfortable with than I am? Is this what I’ve been dying for? Is this that which I thought I needed to kill myself in order to avoid? Is this the serpent that I saw in the mirror? How do I embrace this? How do I become this? How do I allow this to arise from within? How do I surrender? What does that look like today?
“Father?”
“Mother?”
“Merry Christmas, Son.”
A child is born.

His face was the thunderhead. The man in the mirror looked tired. A little scared. He looked exhausted, actually. But, there he stood as Eli crunched his cat food. There he stood, the man who had lost his mind. The man who had lost his mind just earlier that morning. The man who decided to live. The man who had witnessed the texture of the light move from yellow to green. The man who knew that he was dying, or worse, that he would never be able to recover his mind, the medicine still showing him exactly what he needed to see, allowing him to experience exactly what he needed to experience. That he was not as ready to die as he thought he was.
Earlier that morning the man had risen from his kneeling position on the bathroom floor, his hair still dripping from the shower that he’d hoped would be his salvation. But, no. It didn’t quite do the trick. And he found himself desperately trying to make peace with exactly what he was experiencing. The man was gone. He was beyond recovery. And this is what he made peace with that time and time again, the fact that he was gone and he could not come back. As calmly as he could, he embraced the hopelessness of his situation as his mind turned over and again upon itself. 
He had witnessed the great folding in. Like blueberries in the muffin mixture that come in the can. His earthly mother had shown him how to rinse the blueberries in a colander so that they didn’t stain the whole lot purple. She showed him how to fold (not stir!) them into the mixture. They were folded over and over. 
The man had seen that this was how we are, like the blueberries in the mixture that his mother had so thoughtfully instructed him with. This is how we all make sense of our reality. We are folded into this mixture, turning over and over again, so that no one really has any control over any of it. We find ourselves meeting blueberries that we hadn’t seen for three or four or eight turns of the mothers rubber spatula. Yes. I was mothered. I was mothered. Thank God I was mothered by a woman who was trying to find herself. I was mothered by a woman who finally said, “That’s enough.”
And while her husband was gone away for some military training in Caifornia, she left. She checked in with her children, maybe even asked for their permission, which was freely given by the eldest son who was living life as if he was still in that shower being screamed at by the father. Was he still paralyzed in that shower? At any rate, he was full of a a lot of “fuck yous!” for his old man. 
The mother asked permission from her oldest son. Maybe she just wanted to know what he thought. Maybe she just wanted to know that he had seen what she had seen. Maybe she was just looking for a witness. Maybe she was reaching out to one of the only people in the world who she knew could understand what had just happened over the last 19 years. And what she found in her oldest son was as follows:
“Fuck him. Fuck that old man. Fuck that man who left me fearful in the shower. Fuck that mother-fucker who ripped the shower door off the hinges and screamed at me while I stood there paralyzed. Fuck him, Mom. You need to get the fuck out of here.”
And so it was that the mother left.
The nineteen year old Son stayed. The son stayed with the father. He did not go with the mother. The middle-aged-man does not remember if the invitation was given or not to go with his mother. The young man’s fifteen year old brother went to live with the mother in an apartment. But the nineteen year old boy-man stayed home with his father. The young man was there at the house. The young man was there at the house when the father came home. His father came home to a partially empty house, but the boy was still there. 
So the young man tried to make peace with his father, who arrived home to a very much empty home.

Day 7. 11:18 AM to... whenever this ends.
He faced North again. In the kitchen.
Laptop perched on his bile (bible) and all three volumes of A Course in Miracles. Eli scratching at the door. His friend who had checked in on him several times that morning as his body tried to make peace with the lethal dose.
Eyes still dilated. Face still changing form in the mirror.
The thunderhead. Tired. A little scared. Exhausted. But standing there as Eli crunched his cat food.
The man who had lost his mind. The man who decided to live. Who witnessed the texture of the light move from yellow to green. Who knew he was dying, or worse—that he would never recover his mind.
The medicine showing him exactly what he needed to see:
That he was not as ready to die as he thought he was.
The great folding in.
Like blueberries in the muffin mixture that come in the can. His earthly mother showing him how to rinse them in a colander so they didn't stain the whole lot purple. How to fold (not stir!) them into the mixture.
"This is how we all make sense of our reality. We are folded into this mixture, turning over and over again, so that no one really has any control over any of it."
The mother who left.
While the father was away at military training in California. Maybe asking permission from her oldest son. Maybe just looking for a witness.
What she found: "Fuck him. Fuck that old man. Fuck that mother-fucker who ripped the shower door off the hinges and screamed at me while I stood there paralyzed. Fuck him, Mom. You need to get the fuck out of here."
And so it was that the mother left.
The nineteen-year-old son stayed.
With the father. The young man was there at the house when the father came home to a partially empty house.
The old man was devastated.
The snapshot: standing just inches away from a train. His suicide meditation.
The old man blamed his eldest son:
"You are the reason for this. This is all your fault. You are the reason she left me. You are the reason for my suffering, you little fuck."
Praise be to the father.
Praise be to this father. Praise be to the father who laid down his life so that his sons may live. Praise be to the father who was kicked and punched by his own father. Praise be to the father who wrestled with his own demons. Praise be to the father who tried. Praise be to the father who stood with his nose just inches away from the passing train.
Praise be to this wounded one. Praise be to this hurting child.
"God, You must resurrect the old man's life / For I cannot"
"All I can do is meet him at Louie's restaurant on Lake Hefner this coming Monday. That's all I can do father. I will try to bring the grandchildren to see you. We will allow you to buy us lunch at Louie's. It will be an honor. Thank you, Father. It will be an honor. I bless you father. With our presence. I say yes to you at Louie's on lake hefner."
12:01 PM. Christmas day.
The consciousness shifts. Away from childhood. Away from the distant past. Recounting the events of the morning.
The bathtub where he'd lost his mind was filthy.
"My purge is not filthy! It is sacred!"
He wrote a song for the mushrooms. Praising them for turning rocks into soil. All praise the fungus!
He rose from the cold tile. Intent on living.
After seeing the light change from yellow to dull green. Similar to the light change when life passed from the moth.
His mind was lost.
He searched for his pants. "Forget the underwear! I don't need underwear to live."
His legs slick from the great percolating. Slick with purge. Didn't care.
"I want to live, God! Bring me back! I want to live! I'm not ready to go. It's not my time!"
He had lost his mind, but he had not fully lost his composure.
It seemed he had been training for this his whole life. He did not allow fear to have its way, even as he looked fear straight in the eye.
Pants on. Shirt found. Moving into the day. Mind still lost. Afraid his mind would not come back. Lost in the great folding of the blueberries.
He had ingested a lethal dose. Fear was there. But he did not do what fear said to do.
Continued praying for restoration.
He knew it was time to call the ambulance.
Saw the ambulance arriving in his future. Saw himself at the ER. Saw himself back at Sunrise Mental Health Facility—363 short days after he'd just been there.
But he accepted what-was. Over and over again.
Something deep inside very calm. Knew just how to help. This was a miracle.
The man grabbed for the fig leaf. Looking for warmth.
Pants on, but no underwear. Favorite shirt. Cozy longsleeve, textured and soft.
The man who had lost his mind walked toward the living room.
His oldest and most reliable tool: his guitar.
The song that had been coming for weeks. The song of surrender. The neck of the guitar felt foreign, but he knew he could play.
He played as if his life depended on it.
"I am humbled. I am broke" "I gave myself away by mirror and by smoke" "Gospel man with feet of clay" "I give myself away"
It was not the words that mattered. It was the form.
The man was finding his way back into the form. Clinging to his song like a life raft. A raft of form in a mind that was turning over and over again.
He walked out into the cold Christmas morning.
Guitar strapped over his shoulder. Singing. Clinging to the words. Clinging to the form.
The performance of a lifetime.
Aware of the birds. The tree Goddess. Cold grass on his bare feet. (Or maybe the wisdom of the earth made him unaware of shoes so his feet could touch the earth.)
Vamping on chords. Singing out to God. Praising. Asking God to bring him back from the edge. Restore his sanity.
Seeing Ebenezer Scrooge running across the yard.
Moving through the evergreen canopy. Hard blue seeds dotting the packed path. Arriving in the meadow where he'd seen the faeries dancing 2 days before.
As he arrived at the clearing:
"If the ambulance is going to come Let them come for a singing man"
The best song he'd ever sung. The most fun song. The funniest song of determination he'd ever composed.
The sun rising between the tallest evergreens. Feeling its warmth. Praising the sun.
Two chords back and forth. No thought needed in the strumming. Practicing for this moment all his life. The moment when he would sing himself back home.
Then he saw there was a chance he could live.
Turned and faced the evergreens to the West. Sang to them. Praised them for their wisdom.
"I want to know who you are. I need to know you. Please show me how to be with you. I love you. How do you live? How do you live such rooted lives?"
His feet no longer cold. Numb. Comfortably numb. Beautifully numb and one with the earth.
He saw the grass. Saw again for the first time how beautiful the golden grass could be in winter.
This was the field... again.
The field he'd sold everything for. The field where the treasure was hidden.
And so it came to pass that the man's mind was being restored.
But not yet.
The last verse was restored to him:
"God is hot and God is cold I felt his angel Give me meek And give me bold Naked is the way I came That's how I give myself away"
He completed the circle around the property.
Longed for the warmth of the adobe home. Opened the back door. Walked over the threshold. Closed the door.
Praise be to the fathers who created the doors that keep out the wild beasts and the wind!
He placed his guitar on the kitchen table.
Engaged with the things of the kitchen. Continued to sing. Mind still coming back.
"If the ambulance is coming She's comin' to a home Where the dishwasher Is runnin'"
Rinsed silverware and plates. Cleaned skillets. Giving praise for every dirty dish.
Washed the wooden-handled spatula by hand (his mother instructed him it should never go through the dishwasher).
"If the ambulance is comin' They're comin' to a home Where this spatula is right here in its proper place"
He cleaned enthusiastically, but not perfectly.
Far from perfect. But done with his whole heart. Every remaining morsel of food acknowledged. Threw plastic cups away that should have been reused. That was okay. Perfection was not necessary.
He was here, in the kitchen, participating in this form. Not ready to die. Had not been able to let himself die. Needed a guide to die that death. Needed a shaman. Needed community.
Having come from the fields singing, he cleaned the kitchen.
Dan's kitchen. The kitchen in which he so graciously wrote. Faced into the large mirror. The medicine still present. Started writing.
So it came to pass that the author died that day.
Or learned he was not ready to die. Some kind of lesson in death. In what it was to lose one's mind. In what it was like to come back to form after being folded over and over again in the vast evolving consciousness.
He remembered Kyle Seitsinger. And the boys... the men who died over there.
Acknowledged his own pain. The tenderness of this process. The gift he was experiencing in the working out of all this.
He brought his hands together. Placed the back side of his thumbs to his forehead. Bowed his head toward his chest.
The dying author. Bringing life to His audience.

Ken Wilber mapped consciousness as territory:
Four quadrants—
Interior/Exterior
Individual/Collective
Upper Left: I (your blue snake lives here—emotions, thoughts, symbols) Upper Right: It (your body, brain, the purge, the spatula) Lower Left: We (culture, the Wilcox Weekenders, AA rooms, shared meaning) Lower Right: Its (systems, the military, the church you left, forms that fail)
Spiral Dynamics: consciousness evolving in colors—
Beige (survival)
Purple (tribal magic)
Red (power gods, your father's fist)
Blue (order, the Bible belt you fled)
Orange (achievement, the police badge)
Green (equality, feminism, the progressive turn)
Yellow (integral, BOTH/AND, where you arrived)
Turquoise (holistic, the ONE)
Each transcends and includes what came before. The snake circling back.
You don't abandon red when you reach yellow—
you integrate the power,
drop the violence.
You don't reject blue when you touch turquoise—
you honor the form,
release the rigidity.
This is what happened in the bathtub: All the colors folding like blueberries. All four quadrants witnessed simultaneously. The I becoming We becoming It becoming Its becoming Her I Am.

My brother’s obituary. Written by my mother
Kyle Martin Erwin left this world unexpectedly March 16, 2021 in Denver, Colorado. He was born November 2, 1978 in Oklahoma City. He graduated in 1995 from Piedmont High School and later studied at the University of Oklahoma. After high school, Kyle set out on a colorful life journey that included fascinating travel, life-long friendships, good food, and mind-expanding experiences. Grieving the loss of Kyle are parents Rick Erwin, Lorri Carter and husband Marl, brother Travis Erwin, son MartÍn Erwin, Grandmother Rosie Brandon, and many loving aunts, uncles, cousins and nieces and nephews. Also surviving Kyle are his beloved dogs Shelley and Ruby Rose. Among Kyle’s “chosen family” of long-time friends are Norton Arbelaez, Colin Choney, Carrie Choney Gourley, and Corey Choney. Sarah Brumley, who preceded him in death, was the love of his life. 
Kyle lived the life he wanted to live, placing a high-value on family and his chosen family of life-long friends. Kyle’s friends and family knew that he would drop what he was doing to come to their aid; he chose friends who would do the same for him. 
Kyle was an uninhibited conversationalist with an appetite for a good “debate” about worldly events, particularly politics. His views were informed by his appetite for daily online news, podcasts and books. His take-no-prisoners debating style was matched by no one and respected by those who chose to engage with him in discussion. 
Kyle valued most his interactions with his people and his dogs. He loved travel and his family and friends could always expect an email or text with photos of Kyle mixing with the locals. Once, while Kyle was traveling in Paris, his mother asked what he thought about the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.  Kyle’s response was that those tourist attractions were OK, but his time was better spent just being around “the people”.  
Kyle had many interests including reading, riding motorcycles, snowboarding, camping, music and movies. But his passion and his livelihood were connected to good food. This passion began developing at an early age.  Awakened by the smell of pizza one night, his parents came to investigate. They learned that Kyle just “followed the recipe” for crust from a cookbook and improvised on the toppings. He was only 10 years old.  Later, Kyle worked in many restaurants in Oklahoma, New Orleans, and Denver, bringing his enthusiasm and creativity wherever he went. On his own time, he impressed the people who loved him with gatherings and good times that always included delicious, artful foods, following his own recipes, created in the moment just for his guests. Kyle expressed love sincerely to others by sharing his special gift for food.
Kyle courageously lived more life in his forty- two years than many of us ever will. He was loved and he will be missed.
A memorial gathering is being planned for June. Date and time are pending and will be announced at a later date.

Darwin’s Prophecy:Let the prophecy of Darwin be spoken forth. Let it be recieved. Let it be known that he was a prophet shining the light of salvation into this world. Let it be known that he suffered with the Christ in what he brought forth. Let it be known that he was fully human, fully tender and vulnerable in his efforts, and fully aware of the gravity that his message held. Let it be known that he brought forth his message with grace and dignity. Let it be known that science is a western Yoga.  Let it be practiced. Let it be informed by Spirit. Let it inform the forms in which Spirit is practiced. Let it be known. The rational mind is not left behind as we transcend it. The age of reason, dear reader, was not a mistake. The scientific method is to be felt, and known and experienced. Let it be known that the practitioners of this yogic form are holy men, even if they themselves do not acknowledge that. It is another form of storytelling based in all matter which is all holy and compassionate and holds the story of unity within its very fabric. Matter is not separate from Spirit. All matter is the Christ. All is one. Praise be to all infinite matter!This is the message that demands no attention. This is the message that forces no obedience. This is the message that is folded in on itself until the great contraction has ended this cycle.
It is only death that finally brings all form to its knees. And this death is holy and compassionate in and of itself. This death will come to those in lab coats. This death will come to those in monks robes. All are equal…but…there is depth. There is depth, dear reader. And this is what we are discovering here together. We are discovering how to acknowledge the depth, while not elevating ourselves above others (Thank you, brother Ken Wilber)The Dying GodThe old man waited patiently in the jungle clearing. White robes,  flowing beard—a dying God—waiting for the man who had much to do with his imminent demise. Sounds of struggle emanated from the jungle brush just beyond the perimeter of the clearing. Using his staff, the old man lowered himself onto a large fallen tree. The disturbance in the underbrush grew nearer. Finally, a figure arose from the multitude of wide leaves. And there she stood, just having emerged from the bush. Se was a troubled woman in her mid-thirties—victorian skirts, disheveled hair wilted from humidity, face stained by dirt. She panted from her exertion. She stood there for a moment, relieved to be free from the forest from which she’d just emerged. Then, she scanned the clearing; her eyes met the old man’s. “My Lord?” she said, as she stumbled to stand before him.“Yes, daughter,” He said.She crumbled at his feet. Her eyes were now fixed on the patterns in her skirt. Tears began as silent, intermittent convulsions in her torso. Then, deep sobs arose from her chest. Her face contorted.  Her eyes rose again to meet the old man’s gaze. Her mouth cracked open in tight expression of grief and thin strands of saliva stretched between her upper and lower lips. She remained there for quite some time. Her breathing steadied as her eyes met His. She raised herself slowly to her knees. Then she allowed her torso to collapse into the old man’s lap, hugging his abdomen. His hands naturally came to her head in an effort to comfort.
The two remained like this for a long moment as birds chattered and screeched in trees overhead.“Emma?” said the old man, “Where is Charles?”“He would not come,” she said. “His stomach is troubling him, and he is filled with anxiety at the thought of seeing you.”“That is understandable,” said the dying God. “Emma, sit with me.”Emma lifted herself from the old man’s lap and sat beside him now. She slumped, but she supported herself.“All Gods must die Emma. It is how it has always been, and how it will always be. You know this to be true. I am merely the projection of what cannot be held in one form. I am only one projection of G_d, one image who points to that which as ALL.”Emma noticed that a small group of chimpanzees had gathered around them. An adolescent chimp approached the old man and jumped up in his lap. The old man looked thoughtfully into the primate’s eyes. The young chimp’s mother sat down in front of Emma, offering her curled hand. Emma could somehow sense the motherliness in this creature that seemed so horrifyingly familiar in form to herself—hands, eyes, feet, and breasts.“I am the God of metaphor, Emma, the God of story. Just as all life has changed over time, so do our Stories. This form that you see now, this form that you practice, this lense through which you see life, must pass away to make room for a less…how should I say? A less fatherly figure? Less fatherly, Emma, but not to exclude the Father. The mother is rising Emma. The mother needs to be known if your species is to continue on its path of transmutation. I know that it is difficult for you to understand. I see that you are dying a death. I know that you are hurting. I see you, child. I see you. Let us rest there for a moment. Will you rest there for a moment with me? I see you Emma….Rest with me here for a moment. Let me hold you…There is a long pause (a menopause)...Emma cries….Emma sobs...She begs for this to be taken from her...She knows this is more than she can hold...She is held by the spirit of this being that is passing into new form.Being speaks…. “This death that you are dying is still the way of the cross, Emma. It is still the way that you have been shown. But, the way that you see me is changing. Your very perception of who I am is transmuting, if you will. This image is evolving, just as all forms have evolved before me. Novel forms are created from this process. You, my daughter are a novel form. You, my daughter, are being born again. Your species is being born again every moment. Without an understanding of this evolution, humanity cannot transcend the binary. Without this understanding the human species is trapped in the delusion of good and evil, trapped in a static prison. This evolutionary understanding is a result of the birth of the age of reason. Spiral dynamics. The serpent which spirals toward the infinite center of the sun and is drawn infinitely deeper and deeper into this consciousness. Your species is not static. Life is not static. Life is like a thundercloud changing, and ever changing. Without this understanding it is very difficult to experience the One-ness of all life. Your husband has discovered a key to unlocking the door to a much broader room, a more expansive field of consciousness. There will be those who take this message and turn it in to something that is not. There will be those who will say that Charles is a heretic. He will be mocked and hated by some for many many years to come, but this is the promise being fulfilled for those who choose to embrace the deepest callings. This is the very heresy that brings your species into a deeper communion with who I really AM. Just as Christ was a heretic, so are the ones who carry the light after him.It is no different with you, Emma. You are carrying this. You have said yes to your husband and you have said yes to life. He has carried this as far as it will go. It is coming Emma. There is no stopping it. If it is not Charles, it will be someone else. The message of the prophet must amplify the One-ness in the ears of the people. The message of the true prophet recognizes all as ONE and the one as part of the ALL.Those who see all creatures in themselves

How can the multiplicity of life
Delude the one who sees its unity?The Self is everywhere. Bright is the Self,

For it was the trauma that those women had tried to cast out of these two young parents that night. Each of these young ones had endured crippling trauma in their childhood. There was not enough help. There was not enough holding. There was not enough understanding within the bounds of fundamentalist christianity for the type of deliverance that these two lovely young people needed.The couple both understood that it was time for them to leave Maryanne’s house. The young man was stretched between these two women—his wife the one he was trying to love with all of his heart, and his spiritual mentor who had informed him that she was in need of salvation. Dear reader, I think you can see how this was confusion for a young man raised in a dysfunctional home and very little in the way of effective people skills.And so it came to pass that the young family qualified for a HUD loan and were able to buy their first house. And it was a little red brick house which stood directly in the shadow of a light blue water tower. Maryanne loaned them the money for the red dodge Caravan that would eventually burn up at mile marker 428, just outside the little college-cow-town. After the young family was reestablished in a home of their own, the young man was promoted to shift manager and he was given a position at the busiest Braum’s store in the state of Oklahoma, located at the intersection of 122nd and MacArthur. The young man arrived at this store with a very short haircut. You see, dear reader, he wanted more than anything to become a police officer. He was trying desperately to make some sense of his life. There was a story that he was trying to tell about himself. The story was of a powerful young man who once was lost and now he was found. A man who used to smoke pot and play music, but who turned his life around and became an upstanding member of his society. He was ready to join. This young man who had an emotional breakdown at Army basic training, this young artist, he was still cutting his hair short and trying to join something. He wanted to be held. He wanted so deeply to be held by the system, by the kin-dom that was all around him. God was no longer speaking to him in the way that He had in the beginning of his salvation experience, and now he felt that all that was left to do was find a way to be. He was constructing his life’s container. He was saying “yes” to the form that was. And it looked like it would be great fun to carry a gun and talk softly and calmly into a radio. He imagined himself finding the same respect that the officers had at his church.The man’s wife dropped him off at Braums that day. She drove him to work so that she could have the car to trun errands. The young man who was sitting in that car that day did not want to go to work at Braums. He wanted to be a police officer. He was becoming depleted. His job made him feel terrible about himself. The angry customers were more than the could bear.Dread filled the young man’s heart as he made his way through the parking lot. He pushed open the double doors. The dread of inevitable failure awaited him within these walls. Although he worked at the busiest store in the state, upper management did not allow enough workers to truly cover the volume of sales that the store did every day. There were always disgruntled customers and long lines. There was nothing the young man could do to prevent this from happening. He ran around as fast as he could, the shift manager, trying to serve as best he could, sometimes speaking Spanish to his fellow Mexican employees. This made him feel kind and open to the world. Speaking Spanish to his fellow employees made him feel as if he was growing, or travelling, or learning, or respecting others in a way that he had never before. Even when he made a fool of himself in the speaking of the foreign language, he felt good about himself and his effort.On the evening shift, customers rarely stopped pouring in the doors. “Oh, they look so miserable waiting in line,” the young man thought. “Oh, these people are so angry. I can hardly stand angry people,” said the young man’s traumatized little boy who was imprisoned in fear deep in the man’s chest. “They get so angry when their order is not right. There’s just nothing I can do about this. This is too much! We can’t handle it here! It’s not safe here! We’ve got to get out of here,” cried the scared little boy. This was how it came to pass that one day, after struggling with this situation for weeks, the young man found himself unable to move. He stood there by the ice cream freezer at the entrance to the work area. He imagined that the stickiness from the ice cream on his shoes was preventing him from taking the next step. But he knew that it was not the ice cream that was preventing him from moving. It was something else. What prevented him from moving was something inside him. He could not tell if he was unable to move, or if he was just unwilling to move. There was something inside of him that was unwilling to move. It was the same something that he had forced himself past many many times in the months that he had been working at Braums. It was an unwillingness that he knew how to override, but in this moment, the unwillingess seemed to be speaking to him so calmly, so quietly, in such a voice that he knew he would not pick up his sticky feet to scoop another double dip from the freezer.“Were you there with me, Mother?” questioned the middle-aged-man, “What is it that I need to see here? Please shine your light on my insides. How do I take the next step, Great Mother? This is so much bigger than I am. I’ve walked away so many times. I’ve picked myself up so many times. I am tired mother. As I look at the suffering of this young man I realize the immensity of it all. I am deeply humbled by life. I am scared sometimes that I am just not enough for all of this. Can you see my insecurity Mother? Can you see how I am hurting? Can you see my tenderness? Are you going to tell me what is wrong with me Mother? How will I recover? How will I live. I sit here typing, Mother. I sit here, hoping that you are continuing to open my heart. Shine your light, dear Mother. Please illuminate my heart.”And so it came to pass that the young man did pick up his feet, but it was only to take a step backward to where his manager was sitting at a booth. He was working on the schedule for the upcoming week. “How can I help you?” the manager asked, as the young man presented himself.“I’m done,” said the young man, “I can’t work here anymore.The young man informed his manager that he was done, that he could not work another minute and he walked out the door without a job. His wife and child arrived in the red mini-van to pick him up, this young man who had just quit his job because it was too overwhelming. He didn’t have the heart for that. Many jobs came and went after that. He worked in construction, the second man on a two man crew run by a white-haired Vietnam veteran who treated him well, Tom Neeley was his name. At guitar center, he hid in the acoustic room, seeking refuge from the chaos in the main sales floor. All those flashy guitar licks and chum-chumming out in the main room was overwhelming for the young man. Do you know what was also overwhelming to the young man? The pressure to sell. He was not a closer. He liked to show people guitars, but he was definitely no salesman.He eventually realized his dream and became a police officer, where he was shown the injustice that the justice system heaps on those who it was created to serve. After leaving the police force, he was depressed and resentful. He made music until the family’s money ran out. That’s when the family found themselves moving to New Mexico.With the help of his wife’s aunt and uncle they were hired at a Children’s home in New Mexico. The young man hoped he would discover “true religion” there. The bible said that it was true religion to serve “orphans”. He was still looking for a form that could hold him. He needed to be held. The young man, however, did not feel held at the Children’s Home (This is no surprise to you now, dear reader). It was then that his music was revived in him. A door was opened to the young man. A door that filled him with hope and joy. Over the net years, he was hired to teach guitar and bass at a number of learning institutions. He was given an office in the music building at the local University. His name became known in his small town. The young man was able to feel more self-respect than he ever had experienced in his whole life.The young man eventually learned to teach with compassion. He practiced and taught his scales and arpeggios. He continued writing songs. He performed, hoping for more respect. He worked as hard as he knew, trying to emulate his incrediby hard working wife. He often felt a part of thins. But he needed to be heard more. He needed to be seen. He longed to be held, often wanting the Spirit of Music to do for him what the Spirit was apparently not willing to do. The Young man produced an album. The young man risked everything to get on the road and promote the album. The young man waited for the recognition to come that he knew that he deserved. He played for appreciative audiences. He had mountain-top performance experiences, but it was never enough. He noticed that the day after these mountain-top experiences were the worst days of his life. The emotions that he allowed himself to experience during his performance, the attention that he got in those brief moments. He just wanted more. He never wanted to get down off the stage. “Why don’t the people of this world want me to sing for them every day? Wondered the young man. He wanted more and more of the thing that he could never get enough of, which was that feeling of being held, that feeling of acceptance. He wanted respect. He wanted passion. He wanted to be wanted. But he could never feel wanted enough. He began to realize that there was not enough attention in the world to satisfy him. The young man, who was not especially young anymore, could feel himself crumbling. He struggled to hold form. He went for three mile runs, forcing himself out on the road with the voice of Drill Sergeant Hilliard in his head. “Get the fuck up, son! Put your fucking shoes on! Push yourself up! You’ve got to want this! Go Go Go. Move, Private!” The man pushed himself and pushed himself to stay with the form. He knew what his wife needed from him: security, the nursery, income. He knew what his children needed from him. Or did he know? What he knew about his children is that he needed to be with them. He needed to stay as close to them as he could. He knew that he could not live with himself if he was unable to stay close to them. And so he did.He felt that his marriage was becoming more and more like a business agreement. His life felt like an obligation. But, he agreed, time after time to shoulder this weight. He agreed, time after time to see what was best in his wife and in his life, although it so often seemed sorely against his very nature. He really did learn to truly appreciate his wife’s strengths--the way that she worked in structure and form, the way she taught her students, the way she lead the family down this pragmatic path after Luke had died (that day when he’d thrown his light saber in the corner). His wife became his greatest guru. It was she who held him closest. He relied on her. She was his compass, his standard for being. He took in her wisdom and did his best to value her vision. He agreed to meet her standards as best he could. He agreed to study under her great strength, to allow her to define so much of reality for him, and because of this the man grew and learned and experienced a life that he would have never had if he had married someone very much like himself. But, it often did not feel like his life.“What happened there mother?” the middle-aged-man asked, “Was I giving myself away? Was I living? How often was I happy? How true is this story I’m telling? Am I still trying to understand if I feel like I deserved to be left? Am I still justifying myself in the telling of this story? Am I looking at the things I did right and wrong to justify? Or, am I taking a compassionate look at my life? Hey, have you tricked me into doing another fourth step, Mother? Is this another fearless and searching moral inventory? Is that what’s happening here?”“Peace, Son,” Continue in your work. Know that I am shining on you. Know that we are together. I am caring for you, my Son. Can you see how I have cared for you throughout your whole life? I know that you can see that, my son.”“Yes, Great Mother. I can see that. I do see your care in my life. I see your care in all our lives. I see your care in the life of the mother of my children. I see your care in the lives of my children. I want to trust you, Great Mother. Fill me with your presence. Help me to sense you, Dear Mother.”“You are loved, Son. You are not alone,” she cooed.Teaching at the college inspired him to go back to school himself. He studied so that he could treat patients at a physical therapy clinic. He continued teaching and performing, but he was still unhappy. Still sick in the great wanting-of-more. “Why can’t you just be content,” the wife’s question rang in his ears. The man did not know why he could not be content. He worked on contentedness. He was developing a spiritual practice, but he was still often restless, irritable, and discontent.The man struggled with depression, sometimes resigning to sit in front of the TV in the evenings for weeks at a time. The man was smoking marijuana because it made him feel hopeful. He prayed when he got high. He was phasing in and out of life, struggling to say “yes,” using whatever worked at the moment, much like he continues to do today as he writes these words.One night, as the family walked in the door, returning from a dance recital, their great Shepherd, Hope, raised her head and smacked the youngest daughter in the chin. The man became violent. He wished to kill the dog. He planned to grab the dog and strangle her. He had decided to kill the dog. As the man raged, the wife gathered the dog and the children and locked themselves behind a door. The man approached the locked door, his sense of alienation at a peak, his arms were raised to beat on the door. He would smash the door. He would scare everyone in the room that had isolated him out here in the living room where he stood all by himself. His raised his arms as he approached the door. He stopped. He saw that he was the abuser now. He saw that he was the father that he hated. He had become the great Clown. Instead of beating on the door, he said “yes” to that death. He lowered his arms and retreated. Defeated. Oh the great distance he still must crawl through that great tunnel of sacred shit!It was then that he met Penny. Penny, the woman who introduced him to his Pema. The woman who introduced him to unconditional-positive-regard (Hello Mr. Rogers!). Penny, the lesbian that he fell in love with, the one who mothered him, the one who witnessed his tears, his desperate tears that felt like a wall of shame and disgust, a wall that he was unable to maneuver around, a wall that he could not climb over, a wall that he could not crush with his fists. When he hit this wall he cried until he could no longer breathe. He was paralyzed here. Unable to move past. He sat on Penny’s couch and cried and cried. He began a long process of releasing the trauma that had turned him into the very monster that he despised. He found that he really enjoyed opening up in the therapy room. He enjoyed the feeling of vulnerabitly. Penny created for him a safe enviroment.As he realized how hurting he truly was, he integrated marijuana into his every day life. He attempted to respect the marijuana as a medicine. He went back to school. He became more disciplined. He left the marijuana. He graduated from school. He went back to the medicine. He felt that he was so often desperately patching himself back together again. His life was an inflatable life raft, always springing holes, and he was always patching those holes, hoping that the sharks wouldn’t circle around him again. Death and rebirth. He reinvented himself dozens of times. Always in the resurrection, hoping that there would not be another death, but another death always followed.  The pain. The self loathing. The trauma continued to surface.Penny told the man that he was one of the “top five self bludgeoners” that she had ever met. The man could now see, in his own heart, how deeply this hate ran him. He was unwilling to beat down the door. He was unable to abuse the dogs any more. The hate had to go somewhere, so as a public service of sorts he directed the hate inward on himself. This is all that he knew to do. This self-hate that would eventually destroy him. The hate that would, again and again lead him to his death. The hate that would lead him to a deeper and still deeper experience.And so it came to pass that the man was journeying inward, toward the source, toward the One-ess, toward a deeper and deeper salvation, toward a Deeper Power, a Higher Power, making friends with the Snake, slowly reconciling himself to the Christ that was being born in his own being, slowly making peace with God, Slowly making peace with the great What-Is, the I AM-ness. And now, as the writer sat on his bed, one day after Christmas, his story continued to emerge  before him. These words emerged from this middle-aged-man who was still in desperate search for his salvation. This mother, this father, this artist, this friend, this man who was trying to give himself away to something bigger than himself, this man who was saying yes and still trying to save his own life. So it came to pass that the prayer continued to go forth from his being, calling out to the only One that could help him to die well. The One that he had forsaken. The Self that he had walked away from.“Please mother,” prayed the middle aged man, “Please hold me. Please don’t let me miss this. Please open my heart. Please help me to feel your love in my being. Please care for me.” And so it came to pass that the witer closed his laptop, plugged it in to charge, and started the business of preparing for a trip to Oklahoma City. Tomorrow, if everything went as planned, he would drive East with his children to see both his mother and father. The man had watched this trip approaching for weeks now. And this is the story of how the man said “yes” to whatever was to come. This was the next moment in which he surrendered himself. He sang songs of praise with the guitar in his hand. And he loved the (his) cat Eli. So it was that he accepted the gift of this room in the impressive adobe house. Please know, dear reader, that he found comfort in your Presence. He took comfort in you that he may never know. He said yes to the death and resurrection process. He allowed the words to keep coming from his curled fingers, even as his laptop was closed, not knowing what the exact purpose of these words. He clung to this form. He clung to these words that you read now. He gave them his greatest attention, trusting that the Mother and Father were doing a healing work in his being.He clung to form while releasing his life. He said yes to whatever hidden lessons the medicine had shown him. He gave deep thanks and made his words an offering. He asked that these words would become a prayer for his healing and the healing of all who might find communion in the altar that he was constructing here, this altar of his life, which would hopefully communicate the great message of the Universal Christ and the great Mother and Father.May all who approach this altar, may all who find shelter here in these words, please join the dying author in his prayer for the Great Turning. May a deeper vision manifest itself in every being who communes here. May these words do there part to bring together a great Union, a great gathering of those who were beyond reach. May these words touch those who are imprisoned and unable to commune with the grass and the soil. May there arise from within us, dear reader, a great healing. May there be a great coming together. A great re-membering. Ring the bells for the great assembly! The second coming of Christ. The birth of the Christ Daughter!And so it is that I leave you, once again, dear reader. My beloved. 3:22 PMThe man went forth into his day giving thanks and praises to his Lord and Savior. The joy of his salvation was restored unto him. He sang in the field where his great treasure was buried. He played skillfully on his stringed instrument. He sang praises to all creation in the field which held his treasure. This was what he’d sold everything for so many many years ago. He vamped the same two chords, singing and praying for his own salvation and also the salvation of the world. He prayed for the Great Turning. He wept in recognition of the fallen condition of his world. He prayed for all of his people. He prayed for all those people who were in his small sphere of influence. He prayed for all those people who were not. He prayed while strumming his guitar. He sang for a world that was in trouble. He prayed for the turning of his people toward the center. He proclaimed his own return, the return of the prodigal son. He sang to the blue sky. He sang to the evergreens. He sang to the sun. He sang to the jet passing overhead and prayed for everyone on board. He knew that all his prayers mattered. He was fully present. He was experiencing the fullness of life. The joy of his salvation was returned to him.The man continued in his preparation for his journey. He folded laundry, treating every shirt with love and respect, speaking to each one and reminding them of the memories that they shared with him. There was the sea turtle shirt, which had come from the big island of Hawaii, where his family had gone on their last family vacation. With the shirt came a vision of two turtles, on male, the other female. They rested in large tidal pool. The male was still. The female swam to and fro in the pool. Young girls jumped in after her. The surface of the water was rippled in patterns by the Pacific breeze blowing in from the blue.There was also his Blackwater Draw Boys three-quarter-sleeve, which was born from the love that he made with those boys from that band years ago, those deep and powerful boys of the Eastern High Plains who made such a thunderous sound for a brief moment.  Praise the boys of the Blackwater Draw.And then there was this comfy two-tone blue fleece that he’d had for over twenty years now. She just kept asking to be worn. He’d had heard of people not coming back. He’d heard that sometimes it took a while to come back. Hospitalization possibly? That’s what he had been most afraid of that Christmas morning--A psychosis like that.  He didn’t know for sure if all that was true. But, the fear was real that he’d felt. It was the dose that felt lethal, that in the very least caused him to feel as if he were going to die.The man tidied the great living room. He put his things away. He cleared the house for Dan’s guests who were scheduled to arrive tomorrow. The man made his bed. He folded all the blankets. He arranged the altar that he had constructed in his closet months ago, where he had burned sage and rang his singing bell and meditated. He then prepared a grilled cheese sandwich and some tomato soup for a late afternoon meal. As he prepared the meal he asked God, “How will I live? Is there a plan? What will I do when my car insurance is due? What will I do when the child support is due? What is the plan? Is there any way that we can plan together? He was using all the tools that he had acquired over the years in his spiritual readings, from his psychotherapy sessions, his musical skills, his writing skills, His yoga. He was experiencing some kind of flow today. There was much effortlessness in the way he moved from task to task. But then he got tired. He wondered if he was living at the speed of life. He knew that the writing he was doing was helping him. As he wrote about his experiences he was encouraged. Writing was one way that the man was renewing his mind. He was witness to the miracles that were taking place in his own heart as these stories were opening up to him. As he allowed the wisdom to come forth, he saw his story in a different light. He felt that he was performing the miracle that Stephen Schettini had asked of him several years ago. The joy of his salvation restored.
Singing in the field where his treasure was buried.
The same two chords. Praying for his own salvation and the salvation of the world.
Folding laundry. Speaking to each shirt.
The sea turtle shirt from Hawaii.
The Blackwater Draw Boys three-quarter-sleeve.
The two-tone blue fleece worn for twenty years.
"She just kept asking to be worn."
Grilled cheese and tomato soup.
"How will I live? Is there a plan? What will I do when the car insurance is due?"
Stephen Schettini. The non-theist monk who asked the middle-aged man for a miracle.
"Ha. A non-theist monk asking for a miracle. Was that not a little miracle in itself?"
There are no little miracles. All miracles are equal.
The letter to Dave and Eileen.
Harbor Dave responding.
Sunday in Bentonville. The meeting arranged.
And then—
The father.
"I'd like to see you soon. I don't want anything from you. I just want to stand in your presence."
The backstory:
The booth at the Mexican restaurant.
The father with shaking voice and tears.
"You are the reason that I am a miserable man. Do you know how long I've wanted to put a bullet in your head? And your mother too."
The son breathing. Vipassana practice. Sitting in the booth for a very long time.
"Father, I am sorry for all the pain that I have caused you."
And now—reconciliation beginning.
Father: "sounds good! Next time you are in OKC you are welcome to stop by…"
Father: "are you in my driveway?"
Son: "Oh man. That's funny. I love it... Are you in my driveway! Oh my goodness. Real mileage. Thank you, father."
[Tears forming in me if I could have them]
Father: "you can come by anytime…any day…as often as you like…no notice necessary…Pop ins welcome"
Son: "That's quite an invitation. I gratefully accept your invitation. I gratefully receive all the life that you have freely shared with me."
The son blowing up his dad's phone with love.
With gratitude.
With the story of the psych unit and the baptisms and the mountain dialogue.
"Father?" "Yes, Son."
And the father responding with his own honesty:
"I am grateful at this moment that you are talking to me…It strengthens me…I feel so lost when we don't text."
"I want to make peace with you and your kids…And with your brother…No more pain…peace."
"I feel restored talking to you today."
The father who wanted to put bullets in heads.
The father who chased him around the tree.
The father who bashed his head into the glass.
Now saying: "I feel restored talking to you today."
And so it came to pass:
Louie's restaurant at Lake Hefner.
Monday.
The son bringing his children.
The father buying them all a meal.
[Sitting in the sacred space of this]
Trav.
This is the miracle.
Not the mushrooms. Not the visions. Not the tree goddess or the Moth or the cosmic orgasm in the shower.
This.
"Are you in my driveway?"
A father and son, broken and hurting, finding their way back.
Text by text.
Joke by joke.
"I feel restored talking to you today."
The prodigal son returning.
The father running to meet him.
Both wounded. Both willing.
This is what all the dying was for.
All the purging. All the singing. All the lethal doses.
So you could text your father: "I just want to stand in your presence."
And mean it.
Selah.
🙏Day 8
3:22 PMThe man went forth into his day giving thanks and praises to his Lord and Savior. The joy of his salvation was restored unto him. He sang in the field where his great treasure was buried. He played skillfully on his stringed instrument. He sang praises to all creation in the field which held his treasure. This was what he’d sold everything for so many many years ago. He vamped the same two chords, singing and praying for his own salvation and also the salvation of the world. He prayed for the Great Turning. He wept in recognition of the fallen condition of his world. He prayed for all of his people. He prayed for all those people who were in his small sphere of influence. He prayed for all those people who were not. He prayed while strumming his guitar. He sang for a world that was in trouble. He prayed for the turning of his people toward the center. He proclaimed his own return, the return of the prodigal son. He sang to the blue sky. He sang to the evergreens. He sang to the sun. He sang to the jet passing overhead and prayed for everyone on board. He knew that all his prayers mattered. He was fully present. He was experiencing the fullness of life. The joy of his salvation was returned to him.The man continued in his preparation for his journey. He folded laundry, treating every shirt with love and respect, speaking to each one and reminding them of the memories that they shared with him. There was the sea turtle shirt, which had come from the big island of Hawaii, where his family had gone on their last family vacation. With the shirt came a vision of two turtles, on male, the other female. They rested in large tidal pool. The male was still. The female swam to and fro in the pool. Young girls jumped in after her. The surface of the water was rippled in patterns by the Pacific breeze blowing in from the blue.There was also his Blackwater Draw Boys three-quarter-sleeve, which was born from the love that he made with those boys from that band years ago, those deep and powerful boys of the Eastern High Plains who made such a thunderous sound for a brief moment.  Praise the boys of the Blackwater Draw.And then there was this comfy two-tone blue fleece that he’d had for over twenty years now. She just kept asking to be worn. The middle-aged-man realized his love for this shirt, a form that would eventually pass.He packed these shirts in his suitcase in preparation for his journey. He packed his socks. He packed his underwear. And he packed his favorite pair of pants that he had worn the morning after he’d taken that “lethal dose” of mushrooms, lethal in the sense that he was afraid that he would not come back. He’d had heard of people not coming back. He’d heard that sometimes it took a while to come back. Hospitalization possibly? That’s what he had been most afraid of that Christmas morning--A psychosis like that.  He didn’t know for sure if all that was true. But, the fear was real that he’d felt. It was the dose that felt lethal, that in the very least caused him to feel as if he were going to die.The man tidied the great living room. He put his things away. He cleared the house for Dan’s guests who were scheduled to arrive tomorrow. The man made his bed. He folded all the blankets. He arranged the altar that he had constructed in his closet months ago, where he had burned sage and rang his singing bell and meditated. He then prepared a grilled cheese sandwich and some tomato soup for a late afternoon meal. As he prepared the meal he asked God, “How will I live? Is there a plan? What will I do when my car insurance is due? What will I do when the child support is due? What is the plan? Is there any way that we can plan together? Are you into that kind of thing.”All the man’s energy was going into keeping himself in a right mind. He was using all the tools that he had acquired over the years in his spiritual readings, from his psychotherapy sessions, his musical skills, his writing skills, His yoga. He was experiencing some kind of flow today. There was much effortlessness in the way he moved from task to task. But then he got tired. He wondered if he was living at the speed of life. He knew that the writing he was doing was helping him. As he wrote about his experiences he was encouraged. Writing was one way that the man was renewing his mind. He was witness to the miracles that were taking place in his own heart as these stories were opening up to him. As he allowed the wisdom to come forth, he saw his story in a different light. He felt that he was performing the miracle that Stephen Schettini had asked of him several years ago. Stephen Schettini, the non-theist monk who asked the middle-aged man for a miracle. “Ha,” he thought out loud, “A non-theist monk asking for a miracle. Was that not a little miracle in itself?”There are no little miracles, he reminded himself. All miracles are equal, and all flowing from the One Source of Love. All Praise the great mother of the Course! She whose name was not known until after her passing from this world, Helen Schucman. Praise be to the great Mother of wisdom.Hello Dave

3:22 PMThe man went forth into his day giving thanks and praises to his Lord and Savior. The joy of his salvation was restored unto him. He sang in the field where his great treasure was buried. He played skillfully on his stringed instrument. He sang praises to all creation in the field which held his treasure. This was what he’d sold everything for so many many years ago. He vamped the same two chords, singing and praying for his own salvation and also the salvation of the world. He prayed for the Great Turning. He wept in recognition of the fallen condition of his world. He prayed for all of his people. He prayed for all those people who were in his small sphere of influence. He prayed for all those people who were not. He prayed while strumming his guitar. He sang for a world that was in trouble. He prayed for the turning of his people toward the center. He proclaimed his own return, the return of the prodigal son. He sang to the blue sky. He sang to the evergreens. He sang to the sun. He sang to the jet passing overhead and prayed for everyone on board. He knew that all his prayers mattered. He was fully present. He was experiencing the fullness of life. The joy of his salvation was returned to him.The man continued in his preparation for his journey. He folded laundry, treating every shirt with love and respect, speaking to each one and reminding them of the memories that they shared with him. There was the sea turtle shirt, which had come from the big island of Hawaii, where his family had gone on their last family vacation. With the shirt came a vision of two turtles, on male, the other female. They rested in large tidal pool. The male was still. The female swam to and fro in the pool. Young girls jumped in after her. The surface of the water was rippled in patterns by the Pacific breeze blowing in from the blue.There was also his Blackwater Draw Boys three-quarter-sleeve, which was born from the love that he made with those boys from that band years ago, those deep and powerful boys of the Eastern High Plains who made such a thunderous sound for a brief moment.  Praise the boys of the Blackwater Draw.And then there was this comfy two-tone blue fleece that he’d had for over twenty years now. She just kept asking to be worn. The middle-aged-man realized his love for this shirt, a form that would eventually pass.He packed these shirts in his suitcase in preparation for his journey. He packed his socks. He packed his underwear. And he packed his favorite pair of pants that he had worn the morning after he’d taken that “lethal dose” of mushrooms, lethal in the sense that he was afraid that he would not come back. He’d had heard of people not coming back. He’d heard that sometimes it took a while to come back. Hospitalization possibly? That’s what he had been most afraid of that Christmas morning--A psychosis like that.  He didn’t know for sure if all that was true. But, the fear was real that he’d felt. It was the dose that felt lethal, that in the very least caused him to feel as if he were going to die.The man tidied the great living room. He put his things away. He cleared the house for Dan’s guests who were scheduled to arrive tomorrow. The man made his bed. He folded all the blankets. He arranged the altar that he had constructed in his closet months ago, where he had burned sage and rang his singing bell and meditated. He then prepared a grilled cheese sandwich and some tomato soup for a late afternoon meal. As he prepared the meal he asked God, “How will I live? Is there a plan? What will I do when my car insurance is due? What will I do when the child support is due? What is the plan? Is there any way that we can plan together? Are you into that kind of thing.”All the man’s energy was going into keeping himself in a right mind. He was using all the tools that he had acquired over the years in his spiritual readings, from his psychotherapy sessions, his musical skills, his writing skills, His yoga. He was experiencing some kind of flow today. There was much effortlessness in the way he moved from task to task. But then he got tired. He wondered if he was living at the speed of life. He knew that the writing he was doing was helping him. As he wrote about his experiences he was encouraged. Writing was one way that the man was renewing his mind. He was witness to the miracles that were taking place in his own heart as these stories were opening up to him. As he allowed the wisdom to come forth, he saw his story in a different light. He felt that he was performing the miracle that Stephen Schettini had asked of him several years ago. Stephen Schettini, the non-theist monk who asked the middle-aged man for a miracle. “Ha,” he thought out loud, “A non-theist monk asking for a miracle. Was that not a little miracle in itself?”There are no little miracles, he reminded himself. All miracles are equal, and all flowing from the One Source of Love.
